defs: A distributed, append-oriented ledger where blocks of records are cryptographically linked, making unauthorized alteration difficult.

course.learn: A blockchain is an append-oriented distributed ledger in which records are grouped into blocks and cryptographically linked. Changing an earlier record can invalidate later links, making tampering easier to detect.
course.why: Blockchain can provide shared integrity and auditability when multiple parties need a consistent ledger without relying on one central database owner.
course.example: Several organizations record transactions in a shared ledger. Each new block references the previous block's hash, creating a chain of evidence.
course.exam: Do not assume blockchain automatically provides confidentiality or that all blockchains are public. Focus on distributed ledger, cryptographic linking, consensus, and integrity.

course.check_q: Without looking back, explain Blockchain and describe at least two key ideas from this section.
course.check_a: A blockchain is an append-oriented distributed ledger in which records are grouped into blocks and cryptographically linked. Changing an earlier record can invalidate later links, making tampering easier to detect. Key ideas include: Ensure identical information distribution; Encapsulate transactions in interconnected blocks; Detect unauthorized transactions; Utilize hashes for security.
